title: National Quality Framework commences in Western Australia
summary: Western Australia implemented the National Quality Framework through corresponding state legislation, commencing 1 August 2012, seven months after the other jurisdictions.

instruments.title: Education and Care Services National Law (WA) Act 2012

direction_rationale: New national quality standards, staff ratios and qualification requirements raise compliance and staffing costs, which may deter small providers and favour larger operators (higher barriers), while quality ratings give parents more information.
comparison: Other states (treated in FY2011-12 vs WA in FY2012-13)
confounders: mining boom labour shortages in WA
notes: Evaluated 18 October 2026 with monthly and quarterly data (docs/results_childcare_nqf_wa.md, pre-registered, on-off design around WA's seven-month delay): no detectable early effect on childcare's share of business exits (+0.35 points, 90% interval -0.87 to +1.12, base 1.5%) or on child care prices (+0.3%, -2.9 to +5.6); verdict inconclusive, grade Moderate. The direction field remains a hypothesis.

verified.notes: WA date from ACECQA reports (official; read via search snippets); WA Act title not confirmed.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 14-15 October 2026 from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: One national law for childcare quality: national standards, ratings, staff ratios and qualifications replaced separate state rules. Quality ratings help parents compare centres, but ratio and qualification rules raise the cost of opening and running a centre. Western Australia joined seven months after the other jurisdictions.

marks.reason: Adds assessment and rating, documentation and quality improvement planning for every service.
Higher staff ratios and qualification requirements raise the cost of opening a centre, weighing most on small providers.
Published quality ratings give parents information to compare services.
One national framework replaced separate state and territory licensing regimes.

assessment.confidence_note: The archived econometric evaluation found no detectable effect on business entry or exit (grade Moderate).
